description.narrative:
The "Strengthening Civil society for Older people's Rights and Engagement" (SCORE) programme is a 3.5-year global initiative funded by the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) and led by HelpAge International. The overarching goal of the programme is to empower a locally anchored civil society to effectively challenge ageism, amplify the voices of older people, and protect their rights to reduce multidimensional poverty.
Operating across 9 focus countries facing restrictive civic spaces, SCORE focuses on three core outcomes:
Outcome 1. Capacity Strengthening: Enhancing the strategic planning, sustainability, and organizational capacity of national "anchor" civil society organizations (CSOs) to act effectively with and on behalf of older people.
Outcome 2. Stakeholder Engagement: Fostering dialogue and collaboration by generating evidence-based data, ensuring ageing issues feature prominently in national, regional, and global forums.
Outcome 3. Coordinated Action: Supporting older people and their representative organizations to coordinate as active agents of change, holding duty-bearers accountable on key priorities.
A central component of the SCORE programme is the transfer of power to local actors through a CSO-led participatory granting mechanism. The initiative strategically mainstreams cross-cutting priorities throughout all activities, including healthy ageing, secure income, gender equality, disability inclusion, and climate change resilience.

recipient-country.narrative: This activity represents the Myanmar-specific implementation of the SCORE Program. 100% of the funds reported under this activity are allocated to capacity-strengthening and advocacy interventions managed by AGE Myanmar within the country.

sector.narrative: 60% of the activity budget is dedicated to strengthening the capacity of locally anchored civil society organizations and generating opportunities for dialogue and collaboration with diverse stakeholders.
A portion of the funding is allocated to coordinated civil society action aimed at holding duty bearers accountable and increasing older people's understanding of their rights.
Funding supports localized, participatory initiatives addressing multidimensional poverty in older age, specifically focusing on secure incomes, social protection, and healthy ageing.
